tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches

Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Prefer it to 'screenshot' to find what to tap (tap a frame's center), read text, or check a control's state or value; use 'screenshot' for layout, color, and images. Default: the whole visible tree; x/y: the element under that point with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container); marker: the first element whose label (or match_key) contains that text. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted, and text longer than its area shows is cut and ends with ... (occlusion and transparency are not detected); a tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with x/y or marker; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring. Omit for the whole tree, or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type).

{"body":"# Description

Adds two `SitePreferences` custom attributes to control the Environmental Qualities PDP tab per locale in Business Manager, without requiring a code deploy. The SCAPI hook enriches the product response with `c_showEnvironmentalNote` (boolean) and `c_environmentalMessage` (string) based on the request locale.

Closes SFCC-765. Rendering logic is covered in SFCC-266.

# Linked

- Ticket: SFCC-765
- Confluence: N/A
- Figma: N/A

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- Adds `showEnvironmentalQualities` (`set-of-string`) and `environmentalMessage` (`string` JSON map) to `SitePreferences` schema in `system-objecttype-extensions.xml`
- Seeds initial values (`en_FR`, `fr_FR`) in `ZimmermannEU/preferences.xml`; message copy is placeholder pending Dani's confirmation (Jasmijn pinged in SFCC-765 comments)
- Extends `productModifyGETResponse` hook with `getEnvironmentalQualitiesData()` — checks locale against the enabled set, parses the JSON map, enriches response
- `set-of-string` (not `set-of-enum-of-string`) so merchandisers can add new locales in BM without a schema re-import
- `c_showEnvironmentalNote` is always present in the response (defaults `false`); `c_environmentalMessage` only appears when a message is configured for the locale

- [x] ZimmermannEU

- [ ] ZimmermannME (Global-e)
- [x] All sites (shared cartridge / org-level change) — `system-objecttype-extensions.xml` is org-level; non-EU sites are unaffected as the preference is unconfigured and the hook safely returns `false`

entries.name: mcp__ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870__get_design_context
entries.description: Get design context for a Figma node — the primary tool for design-to-code workflows. Returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual metadata that must be adapted to the target project. IMPORTANT: You MUST load figma-design-to-code guidance BEFORE calling this tool. Prefer the /figma-design-to-code skill if available; otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md MCP resource. NEVER call this tool without loading that guidance first — skipping it produces code that ignores the target project's existing components, design tokens, and conventions. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName then use the makeFileKey to identify the Figma Make file. Only for Figma Make files (URLs containing `/make/`), and only when calling get_design_context, assume the nodeId is `0:1`. The response will contain a code string and a JSON of download URLs for the assets referenced in the code. It will also include a screenshot of the node for context by default.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

clientLanguages.description: A comma separated list of programming languages used by the client in the current context in string form, e.g. `javascript`, `html,css,typescript`, etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which languages are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess.

clientFrameworks.description: A comma separated list of frameworks used by the client in the current context, e.g. `react`, `vue`, `django` etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which frameworks are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess

forceCode.description: Whether code should always be returned, instead of returning just metadata if the output size is too large. Only set this when the user directly requests to force the code.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether Code Connect should be used to get the design context. Only set this when the user directly requests to disable Code Connect.

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-design-to-code", "figma-design-to-code,figma-code-connect"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-design-to-code", "resource:figma-design-to-code,resource:figma-code-connect")

excludeScreenshot.description: Whether to exclude the screenshot of the design from the response. IMPORTANT: it is not recommended to exclude screenshots. Only set this to true if the user has explicitly requested it or you are trying to preserve context.

entries.name: mcp__ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870__get_metadata
entries.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

entries.name: mcp__ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870__get_screenshot
entries.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

You are doing an independent code review of a small, already-open PR in this repo (Zimmermann PWA Kit, Salesforce PWA Kit / Chakra UI / TypeScript). Do NOT write or edit any code — read-only review, report findings only.

## Context
PR #111 (branch head commit 6c5297c8, base commit 8ea090a0 on `develop`) implements Jira story SFCC-266: an "Environmental Qualities" tab in the PDP slide-out drawer, shown only on the EU storefront when a site preference `c_showEnvironmentalNote` (a boolean resolved server-side by an SFCC SCAPI hook, per-locale) is true AND there's non-blank content to show (either the product's own `c_environmentalNotes`, sourced from AP21/MuleSoft, or a site-pref fallback `c_environmentalMessage`).

Read the actual diff yourself first:
```
cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa && git diff 8ea090a0f4fbed2090c0cb6caf98e1db4534ffe3 pr-111-review
```
(the `pr-111-review` ref already exists locally, fetched from the PR). The 5 changed files are:
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (the gating logic + tab wiring, around line 830-950)
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx` (new presentational component)
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx` (new story)
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` (mapper: adds `c_showEnvironmentalNote`/`c_environmentalMessage`/`c_environmentalNotes` passthrough fields)
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.test.ts` (mapper test, table-driven)

Also read `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` (specifically `isBlankRichText` and `parseRichText`) since the new logic depends on it, and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductDescription/index.tsx` since `EnvironmentalQualitiesContent` wraps it.

## Rubric to judge against
Read these house rules before judging anything:

# Review — PR #111 (SFCC-266, EU Environmental Qualities PDP tab) Base 8ea090a0 → Head 6c5297c8. Author: Jhoan Dela Cruz. Reviewed by Marcel via zimmerMANNReview, 2026-09-15. ## Findings (verified as I went; own findings, hands-on reproduction unless noted) 1. **CONFIRMED — design fidelity.** `environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx`'s 64px inter-paragraph spacing (`var(--zimm-scale-4xl)` via `& > div > * + *`) produces zero visual effect for the `c_environmentalMessage` fallback content. Verified live on PR preview (en-eu + fr-eu): the CSS rule `.css-18xc9nv > div > * + *` exists correctly in the page's stylesheet and is correctly scoped to the right element, but the fallback string renders as a single text node (`childNodesCount: 1`, `childCount: 0` element children) — nothing for `* + *` to select. File: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx:24`. State: to present. 2. **PLAUSIBLE — extension of #1.** Same no-op likely applies to real AP21 `environmentalNotes` content too, since SFCC-26's own sample value for that field reads as markdown/plain text (`Fabric Origins:\n- Weaving...`), not `

`-tagged HTML. Unconfirmed — no live product in the preview catalog currently has non-blank `environmentalNotes` to test end-to-end. State: to present, flagged as unconfirmed. 3. **CONFIRMED — architecture gap, inherited.** `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx`'s `ALLOWED_TAGS` has no `'a'` entry — any hyperlink (Figma shows "Packaging"/"Emballage" as an underlined link; Jira SFCC-765 comment 14498's sample content authors it as a markdown link) is unwrapped to plain unclickable text. Confirmed via source (no anchor handling anywhere in richText.tsx) + live DOM (no `` in rendered output). Pre-existing shared-utility limitation, not touched by this PR (correctly, per Hard Rule 5 — no refactor-upward) — but blocks part of what the design/content actually need. File: `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:28`. State: to present, framed as a question of intent, not a blocker on the author. 4. **CONFIRMED — test coverage gap.** No test (unit/story/E2E) exercises the actual `showEnvQualitiesTab`/`envQualitiesContent` gating+fallback logic living in `index.tsx`'s component body. Mapper test and story test only the leaves either side of it. CodeRabbit flagged this on head commit today (04:00:04), unaddressed (PR approved 7s later). No PDP Playwright coverage exists at all (pre-existing, documented, accepted repo-wide gap per testing.md). File: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:834-848`. State: to present. 5. **CONFIRMED — lint gate regression, trivial.** `npm run lint`: base 880 problems (827E/53W) → head 899 (846E/53W). +19 errors, 100% in this PR's own files: 1 in `environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx:8` (trailing whitespace), 18 in `productInfo.test.ts:50-69` (table misalignment from the 2 new rows). Auto-fixable via `--fix`. Not CI-gated (lint has no required check in this repo). State: to present. 6. **CONFIRMED — process gap.** CodeRabbit's 2026-09-11 outside-diff finding (`productInfo.test.ts:8`, missing `afterEach(vi.clearAllMocks)`) was never replied to (only the sibling inline finding got a reply). On inspection the suggestion is actually inert here (every `vi.fn()` is a fresh local spy, nothing leaks across tests) — but AGENTS.md requires an explicit reply either way. Minor. State: to present. 7. **CONFIRMED — Storybook convention.** `environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx` titles itself `Pages/PDP/EnvironmentalQualitiesContent`; its three siblings in the same folder (`staticProductHeader`, `detailsAndCareContent`, `pdpFooterLinks`) all use `Commerce/`. Inconsistent with direct local precedent and components.md's own "what does it know about" heuristic. File: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx:12`. State: to present. 8. **CONFIRMED via live browser — AC verification.** AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5 (Jira customfield_10231) verified live on PR preview: AU → no tab (AC3); en-eu/fr-eu → fallback content shown, correctly localized (AC2); tab always last when present (AC5). AC1/AC4 (real notes → tab shows product-specific content) NOT verified — no product in the preview catalog currently has non-blank `environmentalNotes`, contradicting the author's own 2026-09-11 Jira comment (14631) that SKU 4673TS251 has one. Most likely a catalog data refresh since, not a code bug. State: to present as "what nobody verified." 9. **Out of scope, flag only — locale-key doc mismatch.** Jira/SFCC PR#39 describe the BM site pref as seeded with `en_FR`/`fr_FR`; this repo's `config/sites.overlay.js:39-40` routes `/en-eu/` → locale `en-GB`, `/fr-eu/` → locale `fr`. Feature empirically still works live on both routes, so either the SFCC-side docs are stale or there's a normalization step outside this repo — not verifiable from here. Not a PWA defect (PWA code is fully locale-agnostic by design). State: to present to Marcel only, not posted. 10. **Out of scope, flag only — squad-ownership doc drift.** `.claude/rules/squadA.md` AND `.claude/rules/squadB.md` both claim `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` (and `product-list/`) as Squad A territory; CODEOWNERS assigns both to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`. This PR's own body table inherited the (CODEOWNERS-contradicted) "Squad A" claim — explains why GitHub auto-requested Squad B review despite the PR describing itself as Squad A work. CODEOWNERS already correctly gates it; not a defect in this PR. State: to present to Marcel only. 11. **Out of scope, flag only — drawer pagination.** Jira comment (Kiera, 2026-09-07) mentions "pagination... within the drawer" per Figma. Figma screenshot shows `<`/`>` chevrons in the drawer header — generic prev/next tab nav, not content-internal pagination. `ZimmPdpDrawer` doesn't implement these at all (zero grep matches). Predates and is broader than SFCC-266 (whole drawer, all tabs), not in any of the 5 formal ACs — likely belongs to whichever ticket owns `ZimmPdpDrawer`'s header chrome. Not confirmed whether already tracked. State: to present to Marcel only. ## Gates (base 8ea090a0 vs head 6c5297c8, run directly) - tsc --noEmit: PASS both. - Vitest: base 1188/1188 (80 files) → head 1190/1190 (80 files). All pass, +2 tests (the 2 new mapper fields). - lint: base 880 → head 899 problems. +19, all in this PR's own files (see #5). - audit:tokens: 3 unacknowledged violations, identical at base and head — zero new, this PR's new files use zero raw hex/px/rem/em (all `var(--zimm-*)`/`textStyle`). ## Pending - Agent `a341419caed629cc6` (independent correctness/conventions pass) still running — findings to be merged in once verified. - Nothing posted to GitHub yet. Awaiting Marcel's adjudication.

[environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx:24](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx:24) tries to force 64px between paragraphs by reaching in from outside with a CSS selector (`& > div > * + *`) aimed at `ZimmProductDescription`'s internal markup. A second reviewer agent independently found the deeper reason: `ZimmProductDescription`'s own recipe ([zimmProductDescription.css.ts:44](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductDescription/zimmProductDescription.css.ts:44)) already owns this exact spacing value, currently 20px, and its own comment says that number is provisional pending a UI designer decision. This PR quietly overrides that pending value to 64px from a different file instead of updating the one place that's supposed to own it — which is also *why* it's fragile enough to silently no-op. I couldn't confirm whether real AP21 product notes (as opposed to the fallback message) would hit the same no-op — no product in the preview catalog has real notes populated right now to test against, and Jira's own sample value for that field reads like plain markdown-ish text rather than real HTML paragraphs, which would hit the same failure mode. Flagged as plausible, not confirmed.

**2. The link Figma shows (and Jira's own sample content includes) can never render as clickable, in either content path.**
[richText.tsx:28](overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:28)'s tag allow-list has no `<a>` in it — confirmed by both me and the independent agent, and confirmed live (no anchor element anywhere in the rendered output). Any link authored in either `environmentalMessage` or `environmentalNotes` gets silently unwrapped to plain text, with nothing to indicate it happened. This is pre-existing shared code this PR correctly didn't touch, so it's not this PR's bug to have fixed — but it directly blocks part of what the design and the ticket's own reference content need, and it's worth a decision now rather than discovering it in production. Not a security issue — confirmed the stripped attributes never reach `createElement`, so this is a fidelity gap, not an XSS vector.

**3. Nothing tests the actual gating/fallback logic.**
[index.tsx:834-848](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:834) — the two-level fallback (`environmentalNotes` → `environmentalMessage` → hide) and the `showEnvironmentalNote === true` gate have zero coverage. The mapper test only proves the raw fields pass through; the story only proves the leaf renders a string it's handed. CodeRabbit flagged exactly this on the current head commit (04:00 today) and it's unaddressed — the PR was approved 7 seconds later, too fast for anyone to have acted on it. Cheap to fix, and it's exactly the kind of "breaks silently on the next refactor" logic testing.md calls out.

**4. Lint regression, trivial.** +19 errors, both in this PR's own files: one stray trailing whitespace in the new stories file, the rest is a test-table alignment cascade in [productInfo.test.ts:50-69](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.test.ts:50) from the 2 new rows. Auto-fixable, not CI-gated so it won't block merge on its own, but it's a real gate this PR fails.

**5. Storybook category breaks with its own siblings.** The new story titles itself `Pages/PDP/EnvironmentalQualitiesContent`; the other three partials in the exact same folder all use `Commerce/<Name>`. Both me and the independent agent flagged this the same way, unprompted.

**6. Process nit.** CodeRabbit's Sept 11 comment about a missing `afterEach(vi.clearAllMocks)` was never replied to (a sibling comment on the same review got a reply, this one didn't). I checked — the suggestion is actually a non-issue here, every mock is a fresh local spy, nothing leaks. But AGENTS.md asks for a reply either way, and there wasn't one.

### Scope verdict

Correctly scoped. The ticket explicitly limits itself to "conditional render logic and data binding," and that's exactly what this PR does — it doesn't reach into `ZimmPdpDrawer`, `richText.tsx`, or anything else it doesn't own. Findings 1 and 2 above are about content *fidelity*, not scope creep.

### What nobody verified

AC1/AC4 — "real product notes populate the tab correctly" — I could not test end to end. Every product I could find in the preview catalog with the tab enabled falls through to the site-pref fallback message, including the exact SKU (4673TS251) the author's own Jira comment (Sept 11) named as having real notes. That's most likely a catalog refresh since then, not a code bug — but it's genuinely unverified, not just assumed fine.

### What you're missing (not about this PR, but worth knowing)

- **Squad ownership docs disagree with the real gate.** Both `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `squadB.md` say `product-detail/` and `product-list/` are Squad A's. CODEOWNERS actually routes both to Squad B — which is exactly why GitHub auto-requested Squad B's review on a PR whose own body table claims Squad A ownership. CODEOWNERS is what actually governs merge, so nothing is unsafe here, but the two draft docs are wrong and will keep misleading whoever reads them next. If you say nothing, I'll leave it as is — it's a governance doc fix, not something to bundle into this PR.
- **Locale values don't match between repos.** Jira and the SFCC-side PR describe the site preference as seeded with `en_FR`/`fr_FR`. This repo's own `config/sites.overlay.js` routes `/en-eu/` and `/fr-eu/` to `en-GB`/`fr`. It empirically still works on the live preview right now, so either that's stale documentation on the SFCC side or there's a normalization step I can't see from here. Worth a two-minute check with Integration; I have no way to confirm which side is wrong from this repo alone.
- **The drawer chevrons from Kiera's Figma comment don't exist yet.** `ZimmPdpDrawer` has no prev/next tab navigation at all (zero matches anywhere). It's not specific to this tab — it'd affect every drawer tab — so it's almost certainly a different, earlier ticket's gap, not this one's. I did not check whether it's already tracked somewhere.

Nothing has been posted to GitHub. I have a few adjudications for you.

PR comments go to a *different* audience (the PR author, a peer developer), so default to terse there: the ask, maybe the file/line, nothing else. This matches zimmerMANNReview's own stated comment-drafting rules (no opening praise, no jargon-stacking) — the gap was that I wasn't fully applying that rule myself before he flagged it. Applies to inline PR comments and general/review-body comments alike, not just one or the other.

# Review — PR #111 (SFCC-266, EU Environmental Qualities PDP tab) Base 8ea090a0 → Head 6c5297c8. Author: Jhoan Dela Cruz. Reviewed by Marcel via zimmerMANNReview, 2026-09-15. ## Findings (verified as I went; own findings, hands-on reproduction unless noted) 1. **CONFIRMED — design fidelity.** `environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx`'s 64px inter-paragraph spacing (`var(--zimm-scale-4xl)` via `& > div > * + *`) produces zero visual effect for the `c_environmentalMessage` fallback content. Verified live on PR preview (en-eu + fr-eu): the CSS rule `.css-18xc9nv > div > * + *` exists correctly in the page's stylesheet and is correctly scoped to the right element, but the fallback string renders as a single text node (`childNodesCount: 1`, `childCount: 0` element children) — nothing for `* + *` to select. File: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx:24`. State: to present. 2. **PLAUSIBLE — extension of #1.** Same no-op likely applies to real AP21 `environmentalNotes` content too, since SFCC-26's own sample value for that field reads as markdown/plain text (`Fabric Origins:\n- Weaving...`), not `

`-tagged HTML. Unconfirmed — no live product in the preview catalog currently has non-blank `environmentalNotes` to test end-to-end. State: to present, flagged as unconfirmed. 3. **CONFIRMED — architecture gap, inherited.** `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx`'s `ALLOWED_TAGS` has no `'a'` entry — any hyperlink (Figma shows "Packaging"/"Emballage" as an underlined link; Jira SFCC-765 comment 14498's sample content authors it as a markdown link) is unwrapped to plain unclickable text. Confirmed via source (no anchor handling anywhere in richText.tsx) + live DOM (no `` in rendered output). Pre-existing shared-utility limitation, not touched by this PR (correctly, per Hard Rule 5 — no refactor-upward) — but blocks part of what the design/content actually need. File: `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:28`. State: to present, framed as a question of intent, not a blocker on the author. 4. **CONFIRMED — test coverage gap.** No test (unit/story/E2E) exercises the actual `showEnvQualitiesTab`/`envQualitiesContent` gating+fallback logic living in `index.tsx`'s component body. Mapper test and story test only the leaves either side of it. CodeRabbit flagged this on head commit today (04:00:04), unaddressed (PR approved 7s later). No PDP Playwright coverage exists at all (pre-existing, documented, accepted repo-wide gap per testing.md). File: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:834-848`. State: to present. 5. **CONFIRMED — lint gate regression, trivial.** `npm run lint`: base 880 problems (827E/53W) → head 899 (846E/53W). +19 errors, 100% in this PR's own files: 1 in `environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx:8` (trailing whitespace), 18 in `productInfo.test.ts:50-69` (table misalignment from the 2 new rows). Auto-fixable via `--fix`. Not CI-gated (lint has no required check in this repo). State: to present. 6. **CONFIRMED — process gap.** CodeRabbit's 2026-09-11 outside-diff finding (`productInfo.test.ts:8`, missing `afterEach(vi.clearAllMocks)`) was never replied to (only the sibling inline finding got a reply). On inspection the suggestion is actually inert here (every `vi.fn()` is a fresh local spy, nothing leaks across tests) — but AGENTS.md requires an explicit reply either way. Minor. State: dropped — Marcel discarded this from the posted comments (2026-09-15), not worth raising. 7. **CONFIRMED — Storybook convention.** `environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx` titles itself `Pages/PDP/EnvironmentalQualitiesContent`; its three siblings in the same folder (`staticProductHeader`, `detailsAndCareContent`, `pdpFooterLinks`) all use `Commerce/`. Inconsistent with direct local precedent and components.md's own "what does it know about" heuristic. File: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx:12`. State: to present. 8. **CONFIRMED via live browser — AC verification.** AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5 (Jira customfield_10231) verified live on PR preview: AU → no tab (AC3); en-eu/fr-eu → fallback content shown, correctly localized (AC2); tab always last when present (AC5). AC1/AC4 (real notes → tab shows product-specific content) NOT verified — no product in the preview catalog currently has non-blank `environmentalNotes`, contradicting the author's own 2026-09-11 Jira comment (14631) that SKU 4673TS251 has one. Most likely a catalog data refresh since, not a code bug. State: to present as "what nobody verified." 9. **Out of scope, flag only — locale-key doc mismatch.** Jira/SFCC PR#39 describe the BM site pref as seeded with `en_FR`/`fr_FR`; this repo's `config/sites.overlay.js:39-40` routes `/en-eu/` → locale `en-GB`, `/fr-eu/` → locale `fr`. Feature empirically still works live on both routes, so either the SFCC-side docs are stale or there's a normalization step outside this repo — not verifiable from here. Not a PWA defect (PWA code is fully locale-agnostic by design). State: to present to Marcel only, not posted. 10. **Out of scope, flag only — squad-ownership doc drift.** `.claude/rules/squadA.md` AND `.claude/rules/squadB.md` both claim `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` (and `product-list/`) as Squad A territory; CODEOWNERS assigns both to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`. This PR's own body table inherited the (CODEOWNERS-contradicted) "Squad A" claim — explains why GitHub auto-requested Squad B review despite the PR describing itself as Squad A work. CODEOWNERS already correctly gates it; not a defect in this PR. State: to present to Marcel only. 11. **Out of scope, flag only — drawer pagination.** Jira comment (Kiera, 2026-09-07) mentions "pagination... within the drawer" per Figma. Figma screenshot shows `<`/`>` chevrons in the drawer header — generic prev/next tab nav, not content-internal pagination. `ZimmPdpDrawer` doesn't implement these at all (zero grep matches). Predates and is broader than SFCC-266 (whole drawer, all tabs), not in any of the 5 formal ACs — likely belongs to whichever ticket owns `ZimmPdpDrawer`'s header chrome. Not confirmed whether already tracked. State: to present to Marcel only. ## Gates (base 8ea090a0 vs head 6c5297c8, run directly) - tsc --noEmit: PASS both. - Vitest: base 1188/1188 (80 files) → head 1190/1190 (80 files). All pass, +2 tests (the 2 new mapper fields). - lint: base 880 → head 899 problems. +19, all in this PR's own files (see #5). - audit:tokens: 3 unacknowledged violations, identical at base and head — zero new, this PR's new files use zero raw hex/px/rem/em (all `var(--zimm-*)`/`textStyle`). ## Independent agent pass (a341419caed629cc6) — merged, verified Converged independently on #1/#3/#7 above (link allow-list, test-coverage gap, Storybook title) — treated as corroboration, confidence raised. One genuinely new finding, verified myself against source before accepting: 12. **CONFIRMED — styling reaches into a child's internals instead of owning the value in the child's own recipe.** `environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx:24`'s `sx` selector (`& > div > * + *`) overrides `ZimmProductDescription`'s own recipe rhythm (`zimmProductDescription.css.ts:44`, `SPACE_BETWEEN_BLOCKS = var(--zimm-scale-l)`, 20px) from outside the component that owns it. Verified: that recipe's own doc comment already flags the 20px value as provisional and "Owner: UI designer, batched with the 28px/44px gap questions" — meaning this PR made an independent, unreviewed 64px call on a value the codebase's own docs say is still pending sign-off, via a side-channel selector rather than updating the tracked recipe. This is the root cause of #1: overriding a shared atom's block rhythm from outside is exactly the "reaching into a child's internals" smell css.md names, and it's why the mechanism is fragile enough to no-op on single-run text in the first place. Correct fix is a variant/prop on `ZimmProductDescription`'s own recipe (not Tier-1/2-gated — it's a co-located `.css.ts`, routed to the owning squad per overrideStyling.md), not a reach-around from the consumer. Confirmed correct: no other component does this (`grep` for other `sx`-based overrides of this atom found none). 13. Also confirmed via the agent, independently: no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in the chain; `attrs` captured in the parser is only ever tested for a trailing `/`, never passed to `createElement` — the link-rendering gap (#3) is a UX/fidelity issue, not an XSS vector. Graceful degradation confirmed (optional-chained throughout, `=== true` gate fails safe). `PdpFooterLinks`' `triggers` prop derives from the same `pdpDrawerTabs` array (`index.tsx:1189` `.map()` over `index.tsx:887`'s array) as the drawer itself — no risk of an orphaned footer link when the tab is absent. All checked and correct, no action needed. ## Pending - Nothing posted to GitHub yet. Awaiting Marcel's adjudication.

` fallback, both-blank suppression, and priority ordering. - **Storybook title** (the inline comment) — yes, renamed to `Commerce/EnvironmentalQualitiesContent`, matching its siblings now. **Not done:** - **Lint fix** — no. I re-ran `npm run lint` on the new head (`705f1048`): still 21 new errors above current develop's own baseline (929 → 950), up from 19 before. The original two files were never touched for formatting, and the fix commit itself added two more: one in `index.tsx`'s import line (now too long after adding `selectEnvQualitiesContent`), one in the new `neverBlank` test case in `productInfo.test.ts`. Still just `npx eslint --fix` away, nothing structural. Everything else holds: `tsc` clean, Vitest 1229/1229, `audit:tokens` unchanged at 3 (all pre-existing, none new). CodeRabbit briefly flagged a "needs Squad A Lead approval" concern on this same commit and then approved again 18 minutes later at the same SHA, that's it reading the stale `squadA.md` claim I flagged to you yesterday, not a real issue. The PR's actual block is just the missing required Squad B review (CODEOWNERS), unrelated to any of this. Want me to leave a follow-up comment about the lint fix, or are you handling that directly with Jhoan?
